description: @alga-psa/licensing exposes registerBillingCatalogContextLoader(loader) holding one process-wide loader (stored on a global symbol like the existing AsyncLocalStorage so duplicate bundles share it)

isCoManagedPurchaseSurfaceOpen resolves the context from the active AsyncLocalStorage store first, then the registered loader, then (only when no loader is registered) the legacy STRIPE_CO_MANAGED_USER_PRICE_ID env var
When a loader is registered the legacy env var never opens the surface; a loader failure or unconfigured catalog reports not sellable

The catalog context loads at most once per request, and the current seat price is read from Stripe at most once per request. Request scopes: withAuth/withOptionalAuth/withAuthCheck (every server action) open runWithBillingCatalogRequest, a lazy explicit AsyncLocalStorage scope; a server render is one scope through the render slot the server registers (registerBillingCatalogRenderScope with React cache(), from the root layout), which resolveCoManagedRootAccess and EE withBillingCatalogContext join. Inside a scope the EE offer catalog's resolveCurrentOffer is memoised (memoiseInBillingCatalogRequest), so the gate's context load, StripeService.coManagedSeatPrice (no second price read of its own) and preview terms share one Stripe read; catalog writes (setAccountSetting, publishBinding, pauseSales) drop the memo. No memo inside the gate without a scope, no cross-request cache. Measured on one cold /msp/co-managed trial view against the Stripe emulator: the render 1 price read (was 2), getSeatTrialOfferAction 1 (was 3), getCoManagedPurchaseDiscoveryAction 1, getCoManagedPurchaseState 1, previewCoManagedSeatsAction 1 plus its subscription list: 6 Stripe requests per page view (5 price, 1 subscription), was 9 (8 price) on 8ace84ebb4 and 10 in the review guide. A page view is still five requests that each read the price once; at most one per page view would need a cross-request cache or render-supplied client data, neither built
EE surfaceProbe.ts registers loadBillingCatalogContext with licensing as an import side effect; withBillingCatalogContext remains as a per-request memo
Every EE server entry that can reach the gate imports surfaceProbe (server bootstrap/instrumentation path used by server actions, API routes and pages)
The Temporal worker bootstrap imports surfaceProbe so co-managed-seat capability resolution in the worker uses the catalog context
Trial callers (getSeatTrialOfferAction, withTrialIntake, canDiscoverSeatTrial, isCoManagedSeatEligible) return catalog-backed decisions with no change at their call sites
loadBillingCatalogContext logs a caught error once per process per error code (no tenant data) instead of swallowing it silently
currentBillingCatalogContext() returns the resolved context (store or loader) so any reader of price/account identity sees the same value as the gate
